title: Least Privilege and Purchase Guidelines
author: Priya Kapoor
summary: A single-playbook reference describing the company-wide approach to least-privilege access, delegation patterns, procurement approval thresholds, vendor onboarding checkpoints, and travel & expense rules. Includes procedures, an approval matrix, and templates for common workflows.
body:
Overview:
This document defines Redwood Inference's unified approach to three interlocking operational domains: access and permissions (least-privilege first), procurement and expense approvals, and travel/vendor onboarding. The goal is to reduce security risk, accelerate requests through clear routing rules, and standardize evidence for audits.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendor service accounts that interact with Redwood systems and purchasing tools.
- Covers role-based permissions, delegation requests, one-off access, purchase requests (POs), travel bookings, and vendor onboarding controls.

Key Principles:
- Least privilege: grant only the minimum permissions required for a time-bound need.
- Separation of duties: procurement approvals and technical access reviews are distinct steps.
- Evidence-first procurement: every purchase request must include business justification, cost center, and expected deliverables.
- Risk-proportional controls: higher risk or higher dollar value requires stronger vetting and multiple approvers.

1) Access and Permissions (High-level process)
1.1 Request types:
- Short-lived access (<= 7 days): request via the Access Portal and include the task ticket ID. Auto-expire by default.
- Project-scoped role (weeks-months): request via IAM workflow with explicit owner and expiry date.
- Persistent role (product/service account): requires architecture review and SRE/Infra sign-off.

1.2 Approval matrix (access):
| Role requested | Approver | Additional approver when > 30 days or production scope | Minimum justification |
|---------------|----------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| Read-only non-prod | Line manager | N/A | Ticket + task link |
| Write non-prod | Line manager | Security reviewer | Ticket + test plan |
| Prod read | Line manager | Infra owner | Incident/runbook link |
| Prod write | Line manager | Infra owner + Security | Change plan + rollback |

1.3 Procedure (step-by-step)
1. Open a Jira request in project ACCESS with template "Access Request".
2. Fill: system, role, justification, ticket linking to work item, requested expiry.
3. Line manager approves in Jira.
4. If production scope or > 30 day duration, Security/Infra are auto-notified to perform a policy review.
5. Access is granted via IAM automation and a ticket comment includes the principal, role, and expiry.
6. System owner performs an access validation at expiry; automated reminders at T-3 days.

2) Delegation and Emergency Access
- Delegated access (role handoff) must be captured in the Delegation Registry (Confluence table maintained by People Ops).
- Emergency access: use the Emergency Escalation runbook in oncall-and-incident-response.
  - Emergency grants are valid for a maximum of 6 hours, require post-hoc approval from the Engineering Manager and Security within 48 hours, and must include an incident number.

3) Procurement and Expenses
3.1 Purchase request types and thresholds
- Low-cost goods and subscriptions (< $5,000): approve by cost center owner (manager) in procurement system.
- Medium purchases ($5,000–$50,000): cost center owner + Finance reviewer.
- High value purchases (> $50,000): require Procurement lead + Legal + Executive sponsor (VP or above).
- Capital commitments and multi-year invoices: route to Finance for capitalization review.

3.2 Purchase request template (to be attached to every request):
- Business justification (what and why)
- Cost center and GL account
- Supplier name and contact
- Contract term and renewal cadence
- Expected delivery date and acceptance criteria
- Risk assessment (data access, vendor location, business continuity)

3.3 Procurement workflow (numbered steps)
1. Create a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement system with the template attached.
2. Manager reviews and certifies budget availability.
3. Procurement validates supplier, obtains competitive quotes if required (see thresholds below).
4. Legal reviews contracts for > $50k or if vendor will process customer data.
5. Finance issues PO and records commitment.
6. Receiving team confirms delivery and invoices are matched in AP.

3.4 Competitive sourcing thresholds
- <$5k: single-source ok with manager sign-off.
- $5k–$25k: recommend 2 competitive quotes; Procurement may waive with justification.
- >$25k: minimum 3 quotes or formal RFP depending on complexity.

3.5 Expense policy highlights
- Meals: reasonable per diem limits set by region; receipts required for expenses >= $25.
- Air travel: economy for flights < 6 hours; business class allowed with Exec approval or for flights > 8 hours.
- Hotel: mid-market chain preferred, nightly cap by city band.
- Personal expenses (alcohol, minibar, leisure) are non-reimbursable.

4) Vendor Onboarding and Risk Controls
4.1 Vendor evidence checklist (required for vendors that will access Redwood systems or data):
- Company legal name and W-9 / tax ID or equivalent
- SOC 2 / ISO 27001 report or third-party security questionnaire completed
- Data processing addendum (DPA) when vendor processes customer or internal data
- Insurance certificate (cyber liability where applicable)
- Business continuity and backup statements

4.2 Onboarding steps
1. Initiate vendor request via Vendor Portal with supplier profile.
2. Procurement completes vendor due diligence (security, financial, legal).
3. Contract is executed (signed) and the contract is uploaded to Contract Repository.
4. Technical onboarding: obtain least-privilege credentials, register service account, and set expiry.
5. Quarterly review cadence for strategic vendors.

5) Change Management (ties to access & procurement)
- All planned changes that touch production must follow the change-management checklist and be entered into the CHG board (Confluence page + Change ticket).
- For changes that require elevated permissions, a temporary change role is requested with explicit scope, timebox, and rollback plan.
- Emergency changes follow the Emergency Access rules and require post-implementation review within 72 hours.

6) Templates and Artifacts (links and embedded examples)
- Purchase Request (copy/paste JSON example):
{
  "requester": "<name>",
  "cost_center": "<code>",
  "supplier": "<vendor>",
  "amount": "<USD>",
  "justification": "<explain business need>"
}

- Access Request (Jira fields): project=ACCESS, component=system-name, role, expiry-date, justification, linked-ticket.
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (CSV-friendly): vendor, legal-id, soc2, dpa-required, contract-link, insurance, owner.

7) Evidence and Auditability
- Procurement and access approvals are retained for 7 years. Records include who approved, timestamp, and all attached artifacts.
- Automated exports of approvals will be produced quarterly for internal audit.

8) Roles and Responsibilities (short list)
- Requester: submits complete request, attaches required evidence.
- Line Manager: validates need and approves budget/role.
- Procurement: validates supplier and pricing.
- Legal: contract review and DPA owner.
- Security: risk review for access and vendors with data scopes.
- Finance: budget certification and PO issuance.

9) Operational Measures and KPIs
- Mean time to approve low-risk access: target <= 48 hours.
- Percent of access requests with expiry set: target 100%.
- Average cycle time for low-value purchases (<$5k): target <= 5 business days.
- Vendor due-diligence completion rate before first invoice: target 100% for vendors with data access.

10) Exceptions and Escalations
- Requests that need exceptions should include a Mitigation Plan and be raised to the Policy Exceptions board (policy exceptions mailbox).
- Executive exceptions (> $250k or multi-year strategic contracts) require CFO and CEO-level approval.

Appendices:
A. Sample email to request emergency access: "Subject: Emergency access request — <system> — incident <id>" with a minimal payload including reason, requested principal, and expiry.
B. City sleep-band table for hotel per diems (examples):
| City band | Nightly cap (USD) |
| Tier 1 (SF/NY) | 300 |
| Tier 2 (Boston/Seattle) | 225 |
| Tier 3 (mid-market) | 150 |

C. Quick links:
- Access request template: /confluence/eng-infra/access-request-template
- Vendor Portal: https://vendor.redwood-internal.example/
- Procurement playbook: /confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-operations-index

Feedback and updates:
- This playbook is maintained by Finance-legal in partnership with Security and People Ops. For suggested edits or urgent updates, open a page request against this document and tag the owner team.

Change log:
- 2023-05-15: Initial publish (Priya Kapoor).
- 2024-11-10: Added emergency access constraints, refined procurement thresholds, updated per-diem bands (reviewers: Ethan Morales, Sana Iqbal, Liam O'Connor).
